generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table, never NULL; generated rows are appended after the compact rows so PKs never collide with compact PKs.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from the parent table's PK pool restricted to PKs actually present in the written instance (compact + generated); 5% NULL only when the column is nullable; never plant NULL on a NOT NULL FK.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Uniform integer in [1, 6]; never negative. Per-column exceptions override this rule.
generic_sampling_rules.char_enum: Pick uniformly from the enum list defined in per_column_exceptions; canonical values only, no case/whitespace variants.
generic_sampling_rules.char_code: Pick from a small fixed pool of 3-6 short strings; 10% near-variants (case/whitespace).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Pick from a pool of 20 first/last names; 20-40% duplicate share across rows.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Synthesize 'NNN Street Name\nCity, ST ZIP'; 20-40% duplicate share.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Uniform timestamp in [2015-01-01, 2018-12-31] formatted '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; 20-40% duplicate share.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, include L-1, L, L+1 within the column's declared domain.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_text: For each listed literal L, include L and a case-variant (lower/upper).
generic_sampling_rules.tie_order: Ensure at least 3 rows share the tie value at the listed rank; ranks must be reachable at the table size.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: 5% NULL on nullable columns; at least one NULL row per nullable column; NULLs are planted after all value-shaping rules and are never overwritten.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_share: For DISTINCT targets, copy a non-NULL source value into 20-50% of rows; skip NULL cells.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.invalid = 20/20 with reasons compact_rows_missing (20), new_integrity_failures (20), no_rows_added (7); integrity.fk_violations = 553. The writer (tscore_gen/writer.py) is called from cli._one as `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` with no `orig_path`, so the compact database is never copied; instead the writer creates an empty schema and inserts only generated rows. This both drops the compact rows (compact_rows_missing) and, because generated FKs draw from `_parent_pool` which includes compact original values (schema.original_values) that are not present in the fresh DB, produces 553 FK violations.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to the writer (e.g. `write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path=orig)`), or restrict `_parent_pool` to values actually present in the written DB. The instance must be a copy of the compact database plus appended rows, with zero FK violations and compact rows preserved.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_null_rule` plants NULLs on every nullable column using `rng.sample(range(n), k)` with `k = max(1, round(share*n))`, and `_apply_unmatched_join` additionally forces a NULL into every nullable FK. Combined with `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` drawing from `_parent_pool` (which includes compact values), the generated FK columns contain values that are not in the written parent table, contributing to the 553 FK violations. Also, `_apply_null_rule` runs before `_apply_booking_date_rule`/`_apply_room_count_rule`/`_apply_*_tie`/`_apply_duplicate_share`, so planted NULLs can be overwritten by later rules (e.g. `_apply_duplicate_share` copies `col[0]` into `col[1..k]`, and `_apply_apt_number_tie`/`_apply_room_count_tie`/`_apply_gender_tie` overwrite indices 1..2), violating the interface rule that a planted NULL is never replaced.
issues.requested_revision: Apply NULL planting after all value-shaping rules, or make the shaping rules skip NULL cells. Ensure FK NULLs are only planted on nullable FK columns and that non-NULL FK values are drawn from the parent PK pool actually written to the instance.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_duplicate_share` forces `col[i] = col[0]` for i in 1..k on `Apartment_Bookings.booking_start_date` and `booking_end_date` independently, and `_apply_booking_date_rule` runs before `_apply_duplicate_share`. After duplication, `booking_end_date >= booking_start_date` is not re-checked, so the semantic rule can be violated. Similarly `_apply_room_count_rule` runs before `_apply_room_count_tie`, which copies `room_count[0]` into indices 1..2 — safe only if `room_count[0]` is in range, but the tie rule can also overwrite a NULL planted earlier.
issues.requested_revision: Reorder rules so that semantic constraints (booking_end_date >= booking_start_date, room_count in [3,9], bathroom_count in [1,3], bedroom_count in [3,6]) are enforced last, or re-validate after each shaping step. Do not overwrite NULLs.

issues.evidence: Specification `per_column_exceptions` lists `Guests.gender_code` enum targets as `["Male","Female","Unknown"]`, but the semantic rule and `specification.py` ENUMS use `['M','F','U']` (CHAR(1)). The specification's own `uncertainty` note acknowledges this. The atomic-operation extraction also shows `Guests.gender_code` ties_for_order_limit on COUNT(*)/COUNT(guest_id) DESC, which is satisfiable with either domain, but the enum list is internally inconsistent.
issues.requested_revision: Make the enum list in `per_column_exceptions` consistent with the semantic rule and `specification.py` (use `['M','F','U']`), or change the semantic rule and column type. Document the resolution.

issues.evidence: Specification `per_column_exceptions` for `Apartments.apt_type_code` ties_for_order_limit targets `tie_at_rank: [1,3]` with `tie_on: ["AVG(room_count)","SUM(bathroom_count)"]`, but `_apply_tie_order` only forces three rows to share `apt_type_code`; it does not control the aggregate values AVG(room_count) or SUM(bathroom_count) per group, so the tie at ranks 1 and 3 on those aggregates is not guaranteed. Similarly `Apartments.room_count` ties_for_order_limit targets `tie_at_rank: [100]` with `LIMIT(100)` but table size is 15, so rank 100 is unreachable.
issues.requested_revision: Either adjust the tie targets to be achievable at the specified table sizes (e.g. rank within 15 rows), or extend the construction to control the aggregate values per group. Document the intended interpretation.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_aggregate_boundary` forces `apt_type_code[1] = apt_type_code[0]` to create a group of size 2, but `_apply_tie_order` then forces indices 1..2 to equal index 0, producing a group of size 3 — the aggregate_boundary target `COUNT(*) in {0,1,2}` is not actually guaranteed (a group of size 3 exists). Also `_apply_duplicate_share` for `apt_type_code` copies `col[0]` into indices 1..k, further inflating group sizes.
issues.requested_revision: Coordinate the aggregate_boundary, tie_order and duplicate_share rules for `apt_type_code` so that at least one group has COUNT(*) in {0,1,2} while ties at the specified ranks are also present, or relax the aggregate_boundary target in the specification.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_bedroom_different_values` uses `spec.NUMERIC_RANGES[('Apartments','bedroom_count')] = (3,6)` and assigns `lo + (j % (hi-lo+1))`, but the boundary_numeric target for bedroom_count is `[-3,-2,-1,1,2,3]`; the range sampler `RangeIntSampler(3,6, boundary=[-3,-2,-1,1,2,3])` clamps boundary values to [3,6], so the negative boundary literals are never generated. The comparison_boundary target `PRED(bedroom_count > -2)` and `PRED(bedroom_count > 2)` cannot be exercised on the negative side.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the semantic range (3..6) with the boundary literals (-3..3): either widen the range to include the boundary values, or change the boundary literals to values within [3,6] (e.g. 2,3,4).

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_null_rule` computes `share` from `schema.original_values` but the writer never copies the compact DB (see issue 1), so the 'compact share' is not reflected in the written instance. Additionally, `_apply_null_rule` uses `rng.sample(range(n), k)` which can select the same index as a later tie/duplicate rule, and the interface requires 'rows with NULL and rows with non-NULL values' per nullable column — with n=15 and k=1 this is satisfied, but the overwrite risk (issue 2) can eliminate the NULL.
issues.requested_revision: After fixing issue 1, verify per-instance that each nullable column has at least one NULL and at least one non-NULL generated row, and that the NULL share matches the compact share. Add an assertion in the writer or a post-check.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_unmatched_join` plants a NULL in every nullable FK column of every table, including `Apartment_Bookings.apt_id` and `View_Unit_Status.apt_id`/`apt_booking_id`, but does not ensure 'parent rows without children' — it relies on 'natural' unreferenced PKs, which is not guaranteed given the small table sizes and the FK sampling from `_parent_pool` (which includes all compact + generated parent values). The unmatched_join_rows target `parent_rows_without_children: true` is therefore not enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Explicitly reserve at least one parent PK per parent table that is not referenced by any generated child row, and verify it in a post-check.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_duplicate_share` targets `Apartment_Buildings.building_address` with `col[i] = col[0]`, but `building_address` is nullable and `_apply_null_rule` may have set `col[0] = None`; then all duplicated rows become NULL, violating the 'rows with non-NULL values' requirement and the duplicate_share target (NULLs are not duplicates for DISTINCT in the intended sense).
issues.requested_revision: In `_apply_duplicate_share`, choose a non-NULL source value (e.g. first non-NULL index) and skip NULL cells when duplicating.

issues.evidence: Specification `generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity` says 'Uniform integer in [1, 6]; never negative', but `Apartments.bedroom_count` boundary_numeric targets include negative values (-3,-2,-1) and the semantic rule says BETWEEN 3 AND 6. The generic rule and the per-column rule conflict.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify that per-column exceptions override the generic integer_quantity rule, and state the intended domain for bedroom_count (3..6) and how the negative boundary literals are to be exercised (e.g. via a separate column or by relaxing the range).

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/values.py `EnumSampler` applies a 10% near-variant (lower/upper/trailing space) to enum values, including `Guests.gender_code` (M/F/U) and `Apartment_Bookings.booking_status_code`. The specification's `char_enum` rule says 'Pick uniformly from the enum list defined in per_column_exceptions' with no variant rate; the 10% variant rate is only specified for `char_code`, not `char_enum`. This can produce values outside the declared enum (e.g. 'm', 'M '), which may violate the semantic rule `gender_code IN ('M','F','U')` and `booking_status_code IN ('Provisional','Confirmed')`.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the variant rate from EnumSampler (or set it to 0) so enum columns only contain canonical values, or add the variant rate to the specification's char_enum rule and relax the semantic rules accordingly.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_room_count_rule` clamps `room_count` to [3,9] and converts to string, but `RoomCountSampler` already produces strings in [3,9]; the rule is redundant but harmless. However, `_apply_room_count_tie` copies `room_count[0]` into indices 1..2, which can overwrite a NULL planted by `_apply_null_rule` (issue 2). Also `room_count` is CHAR(5) and the sampler produces single-character strings '3'..'9', which is valid but does not exercise the CHAR(5) padding behavior.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure tie rules skip NULL cells; optionally pad room_count to CHAR(5) width to exercise the declared type.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `_apply_booking_date_rule` sets `ends[i] = s` when `de < ds`, which makes end == start; this satisfies `>=` but produces many equal start/end pairs, potentially inflating the duplicate share for `booking_end_date` beyond the 20-50% target when combined with `_apply_duplicate_share`. The interaction is not controlled.
issues.requested_revision: After applying both rules, verify the duplicate share for booking_start_date and booking_end_date is within 20-50% and that end >= start holds for all non-NULL pairs.

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py `build_random_instance` applies `_apply_null_rule` to all tables including `View_Unit_Status`, but `View_Unit_Status.status_date` is the PK and `available_yn` is nullable; `_apply_null_rule` skips PK columns (`cm.pk_pos > 0`) and plants NULLs on `available_yn`, `apt_id`, `apt_booking_id`. However, `View_Unit_Status` has no non-FK sampler for `status_date` in `make_spec_sampler` (it falls through to `_init_sampler` with DateSampler), and the writer's `sample_fresh_primary_keys` may drop rows, reducing the effective size below 20. The `no_rows_added` reason in 7/20 instances suggests some tables (likely `Apartment_Facilities` with 7 rows and composite PK, or `View_Unit_Status`) end up with zero rows after dedup.
issues.requested_revision: Investigate why 7/20 instances have no rows added (likely `Apartment_Facilities` composite PK dedup or `View_Unit_Status` PK dedup) and ensure each table receives at least one generated row per instance, or document that zero rows is acceptable for some tables.
